after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Given that $Q(4,0,-3)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨1,-4,5⟩=-11$, find the shortest distance from $P(-2,1,-1)$ to $Π.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨4,0,-3⟩-⟨-2,1,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨6,-1,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨1,-4,5⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|6\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-4)+(-2)\cdot 5|}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{5}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|6+4-10|}{\sqrt{1+16+25}} \\  & =\frac{|\,0\,|}{\sqrt{42}} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $P$ lies on the plane $Π.$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,-5,4⟩ & =20 \\ 2x-5y+4z & =20 \\ 4z & =20-2x+5y \\ z & =5-\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{5}{4}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $x=2$ and $y=4,$ we get 

$$
z=5-\frac{1}{2}(2)+\frac{5}{4}(4)=9.
$$

So, the point $Q(2,4,9)$ lies on the plane.

$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨2,-5,4⟩.$

after.worked_solution:

\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨5,-1,9⟩-⟨7,-2,8⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨3,-6,-2⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-2)\cdot 3+1\cdot (-6)+1\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-6)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-6-6-2|}{\sqrt{9+36+4}} \\  & =\frac{|-14|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{14}{7} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-7,2,3)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $4x+2y-4z=18.$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=2$ and $y=1$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+2y-4z & =18 \\ 4(2)+2(1)-4z & =18 \\ -4z & =8 \\ z & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(2,1,-2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,1,-2⟩-⟨-7,2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨9,-1,-5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨4,2,-4⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|9\cdot 4+(-1)\cdot 2+(-5)\cdot (-4)|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|36-2+20|}{\sqrt{16+4+16}} \\  & =\frac{|54|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{54}{6} \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
